Sam: FYI we're seeing broken trace propagation for GPU jobs. Spans from runtime don't correlate to gpu-worker spans in Jaeger — most entries show rootless spans. Anyone seen this with Redis pubsub path?
Priya: Do we inject W3C traceparent into the pubsub envelope? If not, context will be lost across async hops.
Jordi: Also check sampling and the collector gateway. Are we shipping OTLP/gRPC or OTLP/HTTP? Collector batching + exporter timeouts can drop/link spans under load.
Marta: I just remembered I rolled out an envoy header sanitization rule to the gpu namespace yesterday. Could be nuking traceparent. Investigating now.
Priya: Common pattern for redis pubsub (python): you need to inject/extract manually when sending raw messages. Example:``` 
# send
from opentelemetry import trace, propagate
tracer = trace.get_tracer(__name__)
with tracer.start_as_current_span("enqueue_job") as span:
    envelope = {"job_id": jid}
    propagate.inject(envelope)  # injects traceparent/tracestate into dict
    redis.publish("gpu-jobs", json.dumps(envelope))
# worker side
msg = json.loads(payload)
propagate.extract(msg)
with tracer.start_as_current_span("gpu_worker_process"):
    # do GPU work
    ...
```
Sam: Runtime is C++ for the serving path — we use our internal tracer wrapper. Need to call the OTEL inject helper before enqueueing into the GPU queue. Right now we only attach job metadata, not the context.
Jordi: If collector is the bottleneck, you might see spans arriving without parents because of re-ordering or dropped parent spans. Check collector logs for "dropped" metrics and the batching processor config (max_queue_size/batch_timeout). Also verify the OTLP exporter timeout isn't too small.
Marta: Confirmed — envoy filter had: `remove_headers: ["traceparent"]` in a header-sanitizer config. Rolling back the change to preserve trace headers and will redeploy to staging.
Priya: For the C++ runtime, ensure you use W3C header names exactly: "traceparent" and "tracestate". Different SDKs accept those by default. Also consider adding a small JSON envelope field like `__trace` that contains the injected headers when passing through systems that rewrite headers.
Sam: Good idea — adding a fallback envelope field for environments that mangle headers. Example envelope: `{ "job_id": "x", "__trace": {"traceparent": "...", "tracestate": "..."} }` so workers can extract if headers are gone.
Jordi: For alerts: create an alert when `otel_spans_dropped_total / otel_spans_received_total > 0.01` for 5m AND `gpu_queue_length > 50` for 5m. Tie that to a Grafana dashboard panel that overlays p95 latency and queue length. That correlates trace loss with backpressure.
Priya: Also instrument runtime spans around kernel launch and data staging: `kernel_launch`, `gpu_wait`, `serialize_output`. Add attributes: `gpu.memory_mb`, `kernel_ms`, `batch_size`. Those make pivoting from trace to Prom metrics easier.
Marta: I'll also make sure envoy has `preserve_trace_context: true` and add an integration test that verifies traceparent survives a roundtrip through gateway -> runtime -> redis -> worker.
otel-bot: deploy-bot: otel-collector config updated in staging (collector/20260318/rc3).
Sam: Nice — I'll run synthetic producer that injects 1000 small jobs with 100% sampling to verify linkage in Jaeger. Will report results. :thumbsup:
Priya: If you need quick Python stress tool, use `examples/trace-prop/stress_producer.py` (hooks into our SDK).
Jordi: After rollback we should also bump collector batching capacity in prod by +20% and monitor `span_processor_queue_length`.
Sam: Ack. Thanks all, I'll follow up with a short postmortem if staging still shows issues.
Marta: rolling back now to staging, will ping when done. :rocket:
